newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add temporary reserves to the U.S. banking system on Tuesday through a round of overnight system repurchase agreements, economists said.

"This morning we're expecting open market system account repurchase agreements. It would appear Treasury balances are coming off a bit; they're fighting between now and tomorrow," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
The Fed's two-week maintenance period ends Wednesday.
"I see a sizeable add need ... It's tight because everyone has a tightening worked into their psychology," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G Lanston & Co Inc.
At 0930 EST/1430 GMT the federal funds rate was at 5-9/16, well above the Fed's target of 5-1/4 percent but only slightly above 5-1/2 percent.
Many market analysts expect the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to raise the funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent at its policy meeting today.
Analysts said the $6.0 billion, seven-day system RP from Thursday was still on the books.

"It's interesting that a few years ago this would have been quite an important Fed move. Their intervention could signal a policy move, but now there's not much going on here other than waiting for the outcome of today's policy meeting," said Flanagan.
Any open market activity on Tuesday will not have any monetary policy implications, experts noted. The central bank's official announcement on interest rates is expected at 1415 EST/1915 GMT.
